title: Цветы от тайного поклонника и допрос Кости  (Flowers from a Secret Admirer and Questioning Kostya)

segments.t: When Elena calls Chef Barinov on the phone to thank him warmly for the anonymous bouquet of flowers, Barinov realizes his gesture worked after all. Meanwhile at the apartment, Nastya eagerly questions a nervous Kostya about whether he spoke with her father and if her parents are coming tomorrow.
Хотел сказать вам огромное спасибо за цветы.
Костик, ну что, не молчи, говори.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
'Hello, Viktor Petrovich, good afternoon.' With the moment and phone in play, Max keeps this short reply brisk and direct.
'Hello. Yes, hello.' With the moment and apartment in play, Barinov keeps this short reply brisk and direct.
Хотел сказать вам огромное спасибо за цветы.

'I wanted to say a huge thank-you for the flowers.' Vika tells Barinov that she wanted to say a huge thank Barinov for the flowers without dressing it up. Even in the middle of the drama, she keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
'You are always welcome for the flowers.' Since Barinov is always welcome for the flowers, Max does not waste words on excuses.

'How did you find out they were from me?' Wondering how Max finds out they were from him is how Barinov puts Max on the spot. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.

'Well, how could I not?' Wondering how she not could cuts straight through the tension between Vika and Barinov. In Russian, she does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
'Just like you.' With the work and phone in play, Max keeps this short reply brisk and direct.
'Thank you so very much once again.' Around the work and phone, Barinov sets a calm, everyday tone with Max. Notice how he sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them.

'Well, did you talk to my dad?' By checking whether Barinov talks to her dad, Vika presses Barinov for a straight answer. In Russian, she does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
'And what did you say to him?' Asking what Barinov says to him cuts straight through the tension between Max and Barinov.

'Did he speak politely with you?' Checking whether he speak politely with Max is how Barinov puts Max on the spot. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is.

'Are they coming over to our place tomorrow?' Here checking whether they coming over to their place tomorrow shows Vika looking for the real truth. In Russian, she does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
Костик, ну что, не молчи, говори.

'Kostik, come on, do not stay silent, tell me.' Realizing that someone come on do not stay silent tell him changes how Max handles the situation. Alright, let's hear the whole conversation once more from start to finish.
Хотел сказать вам огромное спасибо за цветы.
Костик, ну что, не молчи, говори.

That wraps up this scene as elena calls to thank Viktor Petrovich for the anonymous flowers he sent her, and at home Nastya eagerly asks Kostya how his conversation with her father went. See you next time!
